questionText: [Set 47.3] According to the Brahmanical texts (Dharmashastras) on Gotra rules formulated around 1000 BCE onwards:

options.text: Women retained their father's gotra throughout life in all royal dynasties
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Women were expected to adopt their husband's gotra upon marriage, and members of the same gotra could not marry
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Dharmashastras and Gotra Rules.

options.text: Endogamous marriage within the same gotra was compulsory across all varnas
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Dharmashastras and Gotra Rules (Social Histories of Early Societies (Kinship, Caste and Class)):
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 History (Kinship, Caste and Class - Dharmashastras and Gotra Rules):
Two main Gotra rules: (1) Women were expected to give up their father's gotra and adopt that of their husband upon marriage, and (2) Members of the same gotra could not marry (exogamy). (Note: Satavahanas were an exception where queens retained father gotras).

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.
